parole.significato: used in feminine singular forms of most adjectives
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *-at-.

parole.significato: -ness, -ity, -ism, -hood: a suffix forming nouns, especially abstract nouns, from adjectives and other words.
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *-at- as abstract/collective nouns-forming suffix.

parole.significato: The plural ending for most feminine and a few masculine nouns (regardless of state).
parole.testo: From the plural *-āt- of Proto-Semitic *-at- as feminine nouns-forming suffix. Cognate with Arabic ـَات (-āt).

parole.significato: A suffix forming some adverbs from nouns or adjectives.
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *-am, originally a mimated suffix representing the accusative case in nouns.

parole.significato: I ...-ed (used to form first-person singular past from all verbs)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *-ku/*-tu. Compare Arabic تُ (-tu), Aramaic ־ִית (-īṯ)/־ֵת (-ēṯ)/־ִי (-ī), and Tigrinya -ኩ (-ku).

parole.significato: I'll (used to form first-person singular future from pa'al, nif'al, hitpa'el and hitpu'al verbs)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ʔa- (“1st pers. singular imperfect indicative prefix”).
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ʔ-b-d /*ʔbd. See אָבַד (avád) for more.
Presumably denominative from אֶבֶן (éven, “stone”), eventually from Proto-Semitic *ʔabn-.
The "tent" sense is presumably denominal from אוהל (óhel, “tent”), from Proto-Semitic *ʔahl-. The "aloe" sense is thought to be ultimately from a Dravidian language. See aloe.

Usually seen in relation to Ugaritic 𐎜𐎗 (ủr, “warmth; heat”), Akkadian 𒌓𒁕 (urrum, “day”), and Arabic أُوَار (ʔuwār, “heat or blaze of fire”). The “light” senses of course, in so far as one considers where light could intrude in an ancient house—a مَنْوَر (manwar)—, are related to “cave” and “cavity”

parole.significato: Forming words relating to ears and hearing.
parole.testo: Ultimately from Proto-Semitic *ʾuðn-. The sense words relating to balancing comes from מאזניים, see there for more.
From Proto-Semitic *ʔaḫaḏ-. Compare Arabic ء خ ذ (ʔ ḵ ḏ), Classical Syriac ܐ-ܚ-ܕ (ʾ-ḥ-d).

parole.significato: Related to coming after, being behind, lateness, posteriority.
parole.testo: Proto-Semitic, also found in Arabic ء خ ر (ʔ ḵ r), Akkadian uḫḫuru etc.
From Proto-Semitic *ʔakal-. Compare Arabic ء ك ل (ʔ k l), Akkadian '-k-l.
The "God" sense is from אֵל (el, “god”), from Proto-Semitic *ʔil-. Compare Arabic ء ل ه (ʔ l h).
The "fire" sense is denominal from אֵשׁ (esh, “fire”), from Proto-Semitic *ʔiš-.

parole.significato: father (a male parent, especially of a human; a male who parents a child (which he has sired, adopted, fostered, etc.))
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ʔabw-. Doublet of אַבָּא (ába), which was borrowed from Aramaic. Cognate with Arabic أب.

parole.significato: to be willing, to agree, consent (usually with לֹא)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ʔabay-. Compare Akkadian 𒁍𒀪𒄿𒌈 (bu-ʾ-i-tum /⁠buʾītu⁠/, “a thing wished, willed, desired”), Arabic أَبَى (ʔabā, “he rejected, refused, was unwilling, unwilling to do otherwise; originally to hold back, to desire to stay or wish to remain”) and the root ء ب ب (ʔ b b, “to p

parole.significato: stone (a piece of such material: a block of stone, rock or a pebble)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ʔabn-, from Proto-Afroasiatic *ʔabun-. Sense 4 (in board games) is a semantic loan from German Stein.

Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ʔadam-. Comparable to Phoenician 𐤀𐤃𐤌 (ʾdm, “man, earthling”), Ugaritic 𐎀𐎄𐎎 (ảdm, “man; red earth, red ochre”), Old South Arabian 𐩱𐩵𐩣 (ʾdm, “vassals, subjects”), Ge'ez ዶም (dom, “slave”), Akkadian 𒀀𒁕𒄠𒈬 (a-da-am-mu /⁠adamu⁠/, “blood”), Akkadian 𒀀𒁕𒈠𒌈 (a-da-ma-tum /⁠adamātu⁠
From Proto-Semitic *ʔaw. Cognate with Arabic أَوْ (ʔaw) and Ugaritic 𐎜 (ʾō).
From Proto-Semitic *ʔuḏn-. By surface analysis either derived from אָזַן (azán, “to be pointed”) or a primitive word with no verbal root as its origin.
From Proto-Semitic *ʔak-.
From Proto-Semitic *ʔukl-. Compare Arabic أُكْل (ʔukl).
From Proto-Semitic *ʔurḫ-.
From Proto-Semitic *awayat-, cognate with Aramaic אתא (ʾāṯāh, “sign”) and Arabic آية (ʔāya, “sign”).

parole.significato: brother (son of the same parents as another person)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ʔaḫw-.
From Proto-Semitic *ʔaḥad-.
From Proto-Semitic *ʔaḫwat-. Cognate with Arabic أخت.

parole.significato: Lycium (a thorny shrub of the nightshade family)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ʔaṭad-. Cognate with Ugaritic [script needed] (etidu), Aramaic אַטְדָּא and Arabic أَطَد (ʔaṭad).
From Proto-Semitic *ʔayy-. Usually occuring in the form of אַיֵּה.
From Proto-Semitic *ʔayy-; אַי ('ay, “where”) + ־ֵה (e, “hē paragogicum”).
From Proto-Semitic *ʔayyal-.
From Proto-Semitic *ʔayyal-.

parole.significato: A man, adult male human being.
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ʔinš- (“man, person”). See also *ʔināš- (“human”). Compare cognates in other Semitic languages (e.g. Moabite, Aramaic, etc.) ('šm in some).

From Proto-Semitic *ʔanθ-at-. Cognate with Ugaritic 𐎀𐎘𐎚 (ảṯt), Aramaic אִנְתְּתָא (ʾintəṯā), אִיתְּתָא (ʾittəṯā), Arabic أُنْثَى (ʔunṯā). False cognate of Hebrew אִישׁ (ísh, “man”), as Semitic š and ṯ merged into Hebrew שׁ. See female and woman for similar convergent developments involving influence
Related to אֵשׁ (ésh, “fire”), which is from Proto-Semitic *ʾiš-.
From Proto-Semitic *ʔakal-. Compare Aramaic אֲכַל (ʾăḵal), Arabic أَكَلَ (ʔakala).
From Proto-Semitic *ʔuklat-. Feminine of אוכל / אֹכֶל (“food”), or a feminine infinitive form of the verb אָכַל (“to eat”). Compare Arabic أُكْلَة (ʔukla).

parole.significato: god (a deity or supreme being; a supernatural, typically immortal, being with superior powers, to which personhood is a…
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ʔil-. Cognate with Akkadian 𒀭 (ilum), Arabic إِل (ʔil), إِلَٰه (ʔilāh), Aramaic אלה (aláh).
From Proto-Semitic *ʾila (“towards, nigh”), cognate with Akkadian 𒀀𒈾 (ana), Arabic إِلَى (ʔilā).

Proto-Northwest-Semitic *ʾilh, a form of Proto-Semitic *ʾil-, whence also אֵל. Cognate with Akkadian 𒀭 (ilum), Arabic إِلَه (ʔilah) and اللّٰه (allāh), Aramaic אֱלָהָא (ʾĕlāhā) and איל, Phoenician 𐤀𐤋𐤌 (ʾlm), and Ugaritic 𐎛𐎍 (ỉl /⁠ʾilu⁠/).
From Proto-Semitic *ʔalp- (“thousand; cattle”). Cognate with Arabic ألف (ʔalf).

parole.significato: mother (a female parent, especially of a human; a female who parents a child (which she has given birth to, adopted, fo…
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ʔimm-.
From Proto-Semitic *šim.
From Proto-Semitic *ʔamat-. In the plural the two-radical word was enhanced with /h/; compare a similar case in Arabic أُمَّهات (ʔummahāt, “mothers”).
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ʔanāku. The adjectival and adverbial uses are modern innovations.
From Proto-Semitic *ʔināš-. Max Wagner thinks it is an old borrowing from Aramaic אֱינָשׁ (ʾěnāš) under Hebraization of the vocalism.

parole.significato: We; the subject form of the first-person plural personal pronoun.
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Semitic *niḥnu. Cognate with Arabic نَحْنُ (naḥnu).

parole.significato: I (first person nominative singular pronoun, masculine and feminine)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ʔanāku, from Proto-Afroasiatic *ʔanāku.
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ʔasīr-.
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ʔasar-; cognate with Arabic أَسَرَ (ʔasara, “to capture, seize”), etc.
From Proto-Semitic *ʔanp-.

parole.significato: a member Echis genus of vipers
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ʔapʕaw-, compare Arabic أَفْعًى (ʔafʕan), Eblaite 𒉌𒁀𒅇𒌝 (ì-pá-ù-um), and Ugaritic 𐎀𐎔𐎓 (ảpʿ).
From Proto-Semitic *ʔiṣbaʕ-.
From Proto-Semitic *ʾirbay- (“locust”).
From Proto-Semitic *ʔarbaʕatum.
From Proto-Semitic *ʾarbaʿū-.

parole.significato: cupboard, closet, cabinet, or similar piece of furniture
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ʾarān- or *ʾirān-. Cognate to Phoenician 𐤀𐤓𐤍 (ʾrn). Sense 4 is a semantic loan from English expressions like in the closet.

parole.significato: lion (a big cat, Panthera leo, native to Africa, India and formerly much of Europe)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ʔarway-. Cognate with Ge'ez አርዌ (ʾärwe, “animal, beast”). By surface analysis, אֲרִי + ־ֵה.

parole.significato: rabbit (a mammal of most genera of the family Leporidae, with long ears, long hind legs and a short, fluffy tail)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ʔarnab-, attested in the Bible only in the feminine. Compare Aramaic ארנבא (`arnava), Arabic أَرْنَب (ʔarnab).

parole.significato: A female rabbit (a mammal of most genera of the family Leporidae, with long ears, long hind legs and a short, fluffy ta…
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ʔarnab-, attested in the Bible only in the feminine. Compare Aramaic ארנבא (`arnava), Arabic أَرْنَب (ʔarnab).
From Proto-Semitic *ʔarṣ́-.
From Proto-Semitic *ʔiš- (“fire”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒉈 (išātum, “fire”) and Ge'ez እሳት (ʾəsat, “fire”).

From Proto-Semitic *ʔaṯar-. Cognate to Arabic أَثَر (ʔaṯar, “trace, vestige, impression, relic”) and Ge'ez አሰር (ʾäsär), አሠር (ʾäśär, “trace, vestige; way, road; relic”), more closely Aramaic אֲתַר (ʾăṯar) / ܐܰܬܰܪ (ʾaṯar), doublet of אֲתָר (ʾăṯār, “spot, place”) borrowed from it, related also to the v

parole.significato: You, thou: (the feminine singular second-person personal pronoun).
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ʔanti.
From Proto-Semitic *ʔanta. Cognate with Arabic أَنْتَ (ʔanta).
From Proto-Semitic *ʔatān-. Cognate with Aramaic אֲתָנָא (ʾăṯānā), אַתָּנָא (ʾattānā), Arabic أَتَان (ʔatān).

parole.significato: You, y'all, you guys: the second-person masculine plural subject pronoun.
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ʔantum.

parole.significato: You, y'all, you guys: the second-person feminine plural subject pronoun.
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ʔantin.
From Proto-Semitic *bV- (“with, in, at, among”), possibly further from Proto-Afroasiatic *bǔ (“place”).

parole.significato: Related to ceasing, cancelling, being idle.
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *baṭal-.
From Proto-Semitic *bayt-. Compare Arabic ب ي ت (b y t).
From Proto-Semitic *bin- (“son”), *bint- (“daughter”); compare Arabic ب ن و (b n w). A connection with ב־נ־ה (b-n-h, “to build”) has been proposed (see Klein).
From Proto-Semitic *baʕl-.
From Proto-Semitic; compare Arabic ب ر ك (b r k), Classical Syriac ܒ-ܪ-ܟ (b-r-k).
From Proto-Semitic *biʔr-.
From Proto-Semitic *būṣ-.

From Proto-Semitic *buśm-. Compare Jewish Palestinian Aramaic בֻּשְׂמָא (buśmā, “sweet spice or smell”), Classical Syriac ܒܘܣܡܐ (bussāmā, “sweetness, perfume”), Arabic بَشَام (bašām, “balsam; balsam plant”).
The verb “to be idle” is inherited from Proto-Semitic *baṭal-.
From Proto-Semitic *bayt- (“house”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒂍 (bītum), Arabic بَيْت (bayt) and Amharic ቤት (bet).
From Proto-Semitic *bin-. The unchanged form can still be found as a construct in certain proper nouns like יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן־נוּן (“Joshua son of Nun”) or בִּנְיָמִין (“Benjamin”).

parole.significato: to build, to construct, to raise, to erect (a building, structure, or the like)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *banay- (“to build”). Cognate with Arabic بَنَى (banā), Akkadian 𒆕 (banûm), Aramaic בְּנָא (bənā), Ugaritic 𐎁𐎐𐎊 (bny).

From Proto-Semitic *bVʕVr-. Compare Classical Syriac ܒܥܝܪܐ (baʿīrā, “sheep, cattle”), Ugaritic 𐎛𐎁𐎗 (ỉbr, “bull”), Ge'ez ብዕር (bəʿər, “ox, horned cattle”), Amharic በሬ (bäre), Old South Arabian 𐩨𐩲𐩧 (bʿr, “cattle”), Akkadian 𒀫 (būrum, “calf”), Arabic بَعِير (baʕīr, “camel”).
From Proto-Semitic *baʕl-.
From Proto-Semitic *barr-. Compare Arabic بَرّ (barr, “outside, dry land”).
From Proto-Semitic *birk-, *bark- (“knee”).
From Proto-Semitic *baraḳ-.
From Proto-Semitic *wVrrVḳānt- (“green gemstone”), derived from the root *w-r-ḳ ‘to be yellow/green’ referring generically to any green precious stone, including green jasper.
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *bint-, the /i/ changing to /a/ through Philippi's Law and /n/ assimilating to the following /t/. Cognate with Arabic بنت (bint).

parole.significato: virgin (female who has never had sexual intercourse)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *batūl-. Cognate with Ugaritic 𐎁𐎚𐎍𐎚 (btlt), Aramaic בְּתוּלְתָּא (bəṯūltā), Arabic بَتُول (batūl).

parole.significato: Forming words relating to the young of animals.
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *gVr- (“whelp”). Closely related to Aramaic גּוּר (gur) and Classical Syriac ܓܘܼܪܝܵܐ (gūryāʾ, “cub”). Standard Babylonian 𒄀𒅕𒊒 (girru, “lion”) and Arabic جَرْو (jarw, “cub”) are other Semitic relatives.
Proto-Semitic (compare with Arabic ج ن ن (j n n)); the root is known in all branches. The “etiquette” sense is likely a loan from Ancient Greek γενναῖος (gennaîos).

parole.significato: back (the rear of the body, especially the part between the neck and the end of the spine and opposite the chest and be…
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ganb-.
From Proto-Semitic *gubb-. Compare Arabic جُبّ (jubb), Aramaic גב (/⁠gōb⁠/, “pit, moat”), Akkadian 𒁺𒁍 (/⁠gubbu⁠/, “reservoir, cistern”), Tigrinya ጋው (gawə, “cistern”).
Compare Akkadian 𒋢𒄀𒅋𒁺 (/⁠gildu⁠/), Arabic جِلْد (jild), all from Proto-Semitic *gild-.
From Proto-Semitic *gamal-. Compare Arabic جَمَل (jamal, “camel”), جَمَّال (jammāl, “camel driver”).
From Proto-Semitic *gVrān-.
From Proto-Semitic *d-b-r.

From Proto-Semitic *dVbr- (“bee”). Cognate with Classical Syriac ܕܒܘܪܐ (debbōrā), Amharic ዲቧራ (dibʷara), Arabic دَبُّور (dabbūr), زُنْبُور (zunbūr), Classical Mandaic ࡆࡉࡌࡁࡅࡓࡀ (zimbura), Aramaic דְּבוֹרְתָא, זִיבּוֹרָא.
From Proto-Semitic *dibš-. Cognate with Arabic دِبْس (dibs, “molasses”), Aramaic דֻּבְשָׁא, Assyrian Neo-Aramaic ܕܸܒ݂ܫܵܐ (diḇšā), and Akkadian 𒋭 (dišpum).
From Proto-Semitic *dubb- (“bear”). Cognate with Arabic دُبٌّ (dubbun, “bear”).

From Proto-Semitic *dalt- (“door”), cognate with Akkadian 𒄑𒅅 (daltum), Ugaritic 𐎄𐎍𐎚 (dlt /⁠daltu⁠/), and Aramaic דַּלְתָּא. The /t/, which originally marked it as a feminine, has been reinterpreted as the third root consonant and the noun has taken the form of a segolate. Doublet of דָּלֶ״ת (dale"t,
From Proto-Semitic *dam-. Cognate with Arabic دَم (dam).

parole.significato: young sprout or shoot from the earth, sapling, tender grass
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *daṯʔ-.
From Proto-Semitic *halak-. Cognate to Akkadian '-l-k (“related to going”), Arabic ه ل ك (h l k, “related to perishing”).
From Proto-Semitic *šuʔa.
From Proto-Semitic *šiʔa.
From Proto-Semitic *haway- (“to fall, happen, be, become”).
From Proto-Semitic *halak-.

parole.significato: they (the third-person masculine plural personal pronoun, masculine plural of הוא (hu'))
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Semitic *šum. Cognate with Arabic هُم (hum). The central sense is “they”; other senses are by extension.
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *šin. Cognate with Arabic هُنَّ (hunna). The central sense is “they”; other senses are by extension.
From Proto-Semitic *wa. Cognate with Arabic وَ (wa).
The "singing" sense is from Proto-Semitic *zamar-. Compare Arabic ز م ر (z m r).
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ḏiʔb-, with metathesis.

parole.significato: fly (an insect of the order Diptera)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ḏubab-. Cognate with Akkadian 𒉏 (zubbum) and Arabic ذُبَاب (ḏubāb).
From Proto-Semitic *ḏV- (“this”). Cognates include Aramaic דִּי (dī) and Arabic ذا. Compare also the definite form הַזֶּה (hazé) and Arabic هٰذَا (hāḏā).
From Proto-Semitic *zamar-.
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ḏikar- (“man; male; phallus”).
From Proto-Semitic *zamar-.
From Proto-Semitic *ḏanab-. Cognate with Arabic ذَنَب (tail, end).
From Proto-Semitic *ḏaḳan- (“beard”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒅾 (ziqnum) and Arabic ذَقَن (ḏaqan).
From Proto-Semitic *ḏirāʕ- (“arm”). Compare Aramaic דְּרָעָא (dərāʿā), Arabic ذِرَاع (ḏirāʕ).
From Proto-Semitic *ḏarūʕ-.
From Proto-Semitic *zarʕ- (“seed”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒆰 (zērum, “seed”), Arabic زَرَعَ (zaraʕa, “to sow”), زَرْع (zarʕ, “seed”), and Aramaic זְרַע (zəraʿ, “to sow”), זַרְעָא (zarʿā, “seed”).
From Proto-Semitic *habat-.
From Proto-Semitic *ḥabl- (“rope”). Cognate with Arabic حَبْل (ḥabl).
Related to Arabic حَدِيث (ḥadīṯ) and Amharic አዲስ (ʾäddis). Ultimately from Proto-Semitic *ḥdṯ- (“to be new”).
From Proto-Semitic *ḥāmiṣ́-.
From Proto-Semitic *ḥyw (“to live”); cognate with Hebrew חַוָּה (khavá). Compare with Arabic حَيّ (ḥayy) and Ge'ez ሐይወ (ḥäywä).
From Proto-Semitic *ḥdṯ-.
From Proto-Semitic *ḥay(aw)- (“animal”). Cognate with Arabic حَيَوَان (ḥayawān), Classical Syriac ܚܝܘܬܐ (ḥaywəṯā) and Ugaritic 𐎈𐎆𐎉 (ḥwt).
From Proto-Semitic *ḫalap-. Cognate with Arabic خَلَفَ (ḵalafa, “to follow, come after”).

parole.significato: father-in-law, in relation to the bride
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ḥamw-.

parole.significato: jackass, donkey (a domestic animal, Equus asinus asinus, similar to a horse)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ḥimār- (“donkey”). Cognate with Arabic حِمَار (ḥimār). Called after their reddish-brown to gray color, which they share with clay, whose Hebrew equivalent חֹמֶר (khómer) originates from the same root. For a similar etymology, cf. Spanish burro (“donkey”) from Latin burrus (“red,
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ḫamišatum.
From Proto-Semitic *ḫamšū-.
From Proto-Semitic *ḥapar-. Cognate with Arabic حَفَرَ (ḥafara).
From Proto-Semitic *ḫapar-. Cognate with Arabic خَفِرَ (ḵafira).
From Proto-Semitic *x̣arb-.
From Proto-Semitic *ḥaraθ-. Compare Arabic حَرَثَ (ḥaraṯa, “to plow, to farm”).
From Proto-Semitic *ṭāb- (“good”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒁕𒁍𒌝 (ṭābum) and Arabic طَيِّب (ṭayyib).
From Proto-Semitic *ṭiḥāl-.
From Proto-Semitic *ṭaḥan-. Cognate with Akkadian 𒁲𒂊𒉡𒌝 (ṭênum) and Arabic طَحَنَ (ṭaḥana).
From Proto-Semitic *ṭīn- (“clay”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒅎 (ṭīdum) and Arabic طِين (ṭīn). Doublet of טִין
Denominative from יוֹם, from Proto-Semitic *yawm-. Compare Arabic ي و م (y w m).

parole.significato: Used to form words relating to sitting or settling.
parole.testo: Proto-Semitic, compare with Arabic و ث ب (w ṯ b), and Assyrian Neo-Aramaic ܘ ܬ ܒ (w t b).
From Proto-Semitic *yad- (“hand”).

From Proto-Semitic, from an earlier biradical root *yad- (“hand; authority; strength”) (whence also יָד (yad, “hand”)). Cognate with Aramaic 𐡉𐡃𐡄 (yadah, “to laud”), Ge'ez ዋደዳ (wadda, “to join together, establish firmly”) and Ugaritic 𐎊𐎄𐎋 (ydk, “penis”).

parole.significato: Knowledge: that which is known (to a given knower).
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *wadaʕ- (to know), cognate with Aramaic ידע (“know”), Phoenician 𐤉𐤃𐤏 (ydʿ, “know”), Akkadian 𒍪 (edûm, “to know”), Ugaritic 𐎊𐎄𐎓 (ydʿ, “know”), Qatabanian 𐩺𐩵𐩲 (ydʿ, “find out”), and Arabic دَعَا (daʕā, “to call on for help, to seek directions, to find the means or a way”) by metathe

parole.significato: Day: the period between dawn and dusk.
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *yawm-, with monophthongization of *aw. Cognate with Arabic يَوْم (yawm).
From Proto-Semitic *šawmān-.
Possibly cognate with Arabic وَكَلَ (wakala, “to trust”), also found in Akkadian and Ethiopic, from Proto-Semitic *wakal-. Alternatively, Huehnergard and Olyan propose k-h-l as the proto-root.

parole.significato: a (male) child, a (male) kid, a boy (a male child)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *walad-. Compare Arabic وَلَد (walad, “child”), وَلَدَ (walada, “to give birth”), Ge'ez ወልድ (wäld, “child”).

A Northwest Semitic innovation. Compare earlier Eblaite 𒉿𒈬 (wamû, “sea”) which preserves the prototypical /w/ of this root, and distantly related Somali webi (“river”). Cognate with Ugaritic 𐎊𐎎 (ym), Classical Syriac ܝܡܐ (yammāʾ). From Proto-Semitic *wamm- (“sea, river”).
From Proto-Semitic *yamīn-, from Proto-Afroasiatic *yamin-.

parole.significato: to suckle, to nurse, to breastfeed
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Semitic *yanaḳ-.

parole.significato: An owl of the Asio genus.
parole.testo: Probably from the יַקְטוּל of the verb נָשַׁף (nasháf), after bird's calls. Alternatively from the related נֶשֶׁף (néshef, “dusk”). Compare תִּנְשֶׁמֶת. Probably cognate with Akkadian enšūpu/enšūbu (“a bird”) and eššebu (“a kind of owl?”). Ultimately Derived from Proto-Semitic *nVšVp.
From Proto-Semitic *waʕil-.

From Proto-Semitic *waqar- (“to be heavy or weighty; a tree laden with fruits; to be honorable or to hold weight in value”), from Proto-Afroasiatic *waqar-; compare Egyptian jqr (“excellent, worthy”) and Arabic وَقارْ (waqār, “dignity, sobriety”).

From Proto-Semitic *warad-. Cognate to Ugaritic 𐎊𐎗𐎄 (yrd, “to go down”), Arabic وَرَدَ (warada, “to come, to arrive”), Ge'ez ወረደ (wärädä, “to descend”) and Akkadian 𒉿𒊏𒁺𒌝 (warādum, “to go down to lower ground, to come ashore, to go downhill or downstream”).

parole.significato: To flow as water (that is, to rain).
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic, and possibly Proto-Afroasiatic. Cognate with Akkadian 𒉿𒊒 (warû, “to show the way, to direct”), Amharic ወረወረ (wäräwärä, “to throw”) and Arabic روى (rawā, “to relate from memory, cause to memorize, to refer to a source”). Compare with Tigrinya ወረ (wärä, “news”), related to Somali w
From Proto-Semitic *waruḳ-. Compare with יֶרֶק (“vegetation”) and Arabic وَرَق (waraq, “leaf”)
From Proto-Semitic *warḫ-.
From Proto-Semitic *waraḳ-.

parole.significato: orphan (person whose either parent has died)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *yatam- (“to be fatherless or without a guardian, to be without support of family or tribe, to be disenfranchised or alone”). Cognate with Arabic يَتِيم (yatīm), Aramaic יַתְמָא (yaṯmā), Classical Syriac ܝܲܬ݂ܡܵܐ (yaṯmā), Classical Mandaic ࡉࡀࡕࡉࡌࡀ (yatima), Phoenician 𐤉‬𐤕‬𐤌 (y‬t‬m‬)

parole.significato: Forms words meaning or related to the following.
parole.testo: From the Proto-Semitic *kabid- (“liver”). Compare with Akkadian 𒂂 (kabtum), Ugaritic 𐎋𐎁𐎄 (kbd), and Arabic كَبِد (kabid)

parole.significato: Forming words relating to firmness, establishment.
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *kawan- (“to be in a place, to happen or occur, to be present”). Compare Aramaic כַּוֵּן (“to be straightened, to be made right”), Arabic ك و ن (k-w-n, “root relating to existence”), Akkadian 𒄀 (kânum, “to be firm, to hold true”), Ge'ez ኮነ (konä, “to be”), Old South Arabian 𐩫𐩥𐩬 (k

From Proto-Semitic *kabid- (“liver”), which literally means "heavy (one)", since when washing the internal organs of slaughtered animals the liver sinks to the bottom. Compare the similar etymology of Russian лёгкое (ljóxkoje, “lung”), directly from лёгкий (ljóxkij, “light”), because in contrast to
From Proto-Semitic, cognate with Akkadian 𒂂 (kabtum), Ugaritic 𐎋𐎁𐎄 (kbd), Arabic كَبِد (kabid) and Ge'ez ክቡድ (kəbud).

parole.significato: A Jewish priest, a cohen or kohen: a patrilineal descendant of the Biblical Aaron.
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Semitic *kāhin-; compare Aramaic כהנא (kāhnā), Ugaritic 𐎋𐎅𐎐 (khn), Phoenician 𐤊𐤄𐤍 (khn), Classical Syriac ܟܗܢܐ (kāhnā), Arabic كَاهِن (kāhin), Ge'ez ካህን (kahn), Mandaic ࡊࡀࡄࡍࡀ (kahna).

parole.significato: star (any small, natural and bright dot in the sky, most visible in the night or twilight sky)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *kabkab-. Cognate with Ge'ez ኮከብ (kokäb). The senses relating to fame are a semantic loan from English star.
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *kaʔs- (“cup”).
From Proto-Semitic *kiyā.
From Proto-Semitic *kinnār-.
From a Proto-Semitic root, cognate with Arabic كَفَّرَ (kaffara, “to cover, expiate, forgive”).

parole.significato: All, whole, entirety, everything; found almost exclusively in singular definite and singular construct forms; used to t…
parole.testo: Compare Arabic كُلّ (kull), Ge'ez ኵል (kʷəll), Ugaritic 𐎋𐎍 (kl), Phoenician 𐤊𐤋 (kl), Akkadian 𒆕𒀀𒁉 (kalûm), Classical Syriac ܟܾܠ (kul), Amharic ሁሉ (hulu). From Proto-Semitic *kʷall- or Proto-Semitic *kull-, ultimately from Proto-Afroasiatic *ʔa-kʷall-.

parole.significato: dog (the species Canis familiaris (sometimes designated Canis lupus familiaris), domesticated for thousands of years an…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Semitic *kalb-.
From Proto-Semitic *kanap-, cognate with Akkadian 𒉺 (kappum, “wing, branch”), Arabic كَنَف (kanaf, “wing, side, bosom”), Ge'ez ክንፍ (kənf, “wing, fin”), Amharic ክንፍ (kənf, “wing”).
From Proto-Semitic *kapp-. Cognate with Arabic كَفّ (kaff).
From a Proto-Semitic source akin to Akkadian 𒅗𒊒𒁍 (“to bless”), 𒅗𒊑𒁍 (“one who blesses”).
From Proto-Semitic *kariś-. Cognate with Arabic كَرِش (kariš) and Aramaic כַּרְסָא (karsā).

parole.significato: To; the first part of a to-infinitive.
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *lV-.

parole.significato: Not; used in negating verbs, adjectives, and adverbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *lā. Cognate with Arabic لا.

parole.significato: heart (a muscular organ that pumps blood through the body, traditionally thought to be the seat of emotion)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *libb-. Cognate with Aramaic לִבָּא (libbā), Arabic لُبّ (lubb), Amharic ልብ (ləbb).
From the root ל־ב־ב (l-b-b). From Proto-Semitic *libb-.
From Proto-Semitic *labiʔ- (“lion”).
From Proto-Semitic *labiʾ- (“lion”).
Inherited from Proto-Semitic. Compare Arabic لَبَسَ (labasa).
From Proto-Semitic *layl- (“night”). Cognate with Arabic لَيْل (layl, “nighttime”).

parole.significato: night (the time when the Sun is below the horizon when the sky is dark)
parole.testo: Likely a remnant of the accusative case (used adverbially to mean “at night”) of לַיִל (láyil), from Proto-Semitic *layl-. Cognate with Arabic لَيْل (layl), لَيْلَة (layla), Aramaic לֵילְיָא (lēləyā), Classical Syriac ܠܹܠܝܵܐ (lēlyā).
From Proto-Semitic *layṯ- (“lion”). Cognate with Arabic لَيْث (layṯ, “lion”) and Aramaic לֵיתָא (lēṯā, “lion”).

parole.significato: turnip (the white root of a yellow-flowered plant, Brassica rapa, grown as a vegetable and as fodder for cattle)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *lapt-.
Inherited from Proto-Semitic, from Proto-Afroasiatic, ultimately of onomatopoeic origin. Cognate with Arabic لَقَّ (laqqa, “to lap”) and Tashelhit llɣ (“to lick, lap”).
From Proto-Semitic *lawaṯ-.
From Proto-Semitic *lišān-.
From Proto-Semitic *ma-.
From Proto-Semitic *mawut-. Compare Classical Syriac ܡ ܘ ܬ, Arabic م و ت (m w t), Akkadian m-w-t.

parole.significato: Relating to reigning, to being king.
parole.testo: See Proto-Semitic *malk-; cognate with Arabic م ل ك (mlk, “to reign, to possess”)
From Proto-Semitic *miʾat-.
From Proto-Semitic Proto-Semitic *madbar- (“pasturage”), from *ma- + *d-b-r. By surface analysis, מִ־ + ד־ב־ר. Originally meaning "place to which livestock are driven for pasture."

parole.significato: To measure: to determine the size of.
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *mdd (“stretch, spread, measure”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒉘 (madādum) and Arabic مَدَّ (madda).
From Proto-Semitic *muḫḫ- (“head; brain; marrow”).
From Proto-Semitic [Term?]. Compare Aramaic ܡܛܪܐ, מִטְרָא (miṭrā), Arabic مَطَر (maṭar).
From Proto-Semitic *māy-. Compare Aramaic מַיָּא (mayyā), Arabic مَاء (māʔ). Doublet of מ״ם (“מ”).
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *malk-. Cognate to Aramaic מַלְכָּא (malkā, “king”), Arabic مَلِك (malik, “king”) and Akkadian 𒂷𒆪 (malku, “prince”).
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *miʕay-.
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *mṯ̣ʔ (“to reach”). Compare Ge'ez መጽአ (mäṣʾä, “to come”).

parole.significato: a rebellion, insurrection, mutiny, an uprising
parole.testo: From the root מ־ר־ד (m-r-d), from Proto-Semitic *marad- (“to fortify, to set up resistance; to escape, to find a means to get away; to leave one's people, to branch off or split from a group”). Cognate with Aramaic מִרְדָּא (mirdā), Classical Syriac ܡܪܕܐ (merdā), Classical Mandaic ࡌࡉࡓࡃࡀ (mirda) and

From Proto-Semitic *marad- (“to fortify, to set up resistance; to escape, to find a means to get away; to leave one's people, to branch off or split from a group”). Cognate with Arabic تمرد (tamarrada), Aramaic מִרְדָּא (mirdā), Classical Syriac ܡܪܕܐ (merdā), Classical Mandaic ࡌࡉࡓࡃࡀ (MYRDʾ).
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *mawut-. Cognate with Arabic مَاتَ (māta), Ge'ez ሞተ (motä), Egyptian mwt, Akkadian 𒈪𒌈 (mītum).

parole.significato: Sweet: having a pleasant taste, akin to that of sugar.
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *matḳ-. Compare Ugaritic 𐎎𐎚𐎖 (mtq).
From Proto-Semitic *mut-.
From Proto-Semitic *nahar- (“river”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒀀𒇉 (nārum) and Arabic نَهْر (nahr). The verb is a denominal and follows from the noun, cf. Arabic نَهَرَ (nahara, “to flow”).
From Proto-Semitic *naḳad- (“sheep, shepherd”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒈾𒆤 (nāqidum) and Ugaritic 𐎐𐎖𐎄 (nqd).
From Proto-Semitic *nūr-, via Aramaic נוּר (“fire”). Cognate with Arabic نُور (nūr, “light”) and نَار (nār, “fire”).

parole.significato: We; the subject form of the first-person plural personal pronoun.
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *niḥnu. Relationship with אֲנַחְנוּ disputed, * According to Ibn Ezra, the original/archaic form of אֲנַחְנוּ. * According to BDB, an abbreviated form of אֲנַחְנוּ. * Others suggest נַחְנוּ is a dialectal or poetic variant.

parole.significato: snake (any of the suborder Serpentes of legless reptiles with long, thin bodies and fork-shaped tongues)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *naḥaš- (“lion”). Compare Arabic حَنَش (ḥanaš, “snake”), Akkadian 𒌨𒈤𒊭𒆕𒋡𒊑 (nēšu ša qaqqari, “snake, chameleon”, literally “lion of the ground”) and Ugaritic 𐎐𐎈𐎌 (nḥš, “snake”).
Geminate stem from Proto-Semitic *nadaw- (“to call out”).
From Proto-Semitic *nūr-.
From Proto-Semitic *namir-, from Proto-Afroasiatic *mary-. Cognate with Arabic نَمِر (namir) and Aramaic נִמְרָא (nimrā).

parole.significato: a sieve (device to separate larger objects)
parole.testo: The root is inherited from Proto-Semitic *npy (“to sieve”). Compare Akkadian 𒈾𒁍𒌋 (/⁠napû⁠/, “to sift”), Jewish Palestinian Aramaic נפי (npy /⁠nāpī⁠/, “to fan, winnow, sift”), and Arabic ن ف ي (n f y).
From Proto-Semitic *napaḫ-, which is of onomatopoeic origin and imitates the sound of blowing air out.

parole.significato: a soul, psyche (spirit of a person or animal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *napš-. Compare Akkadian 𒆒 (napāšum, “to breathe”), 𒍣 (napištum, “life”), Arabic نَفْس (nafs, “a soul, a life”), and Ge'ez ነፍስ (näfs). Compare נָשַׁף (nasháf, “to blow”) and נָשַׁם (nashám, “to breathe”).

parole.significato: candle (a light source consisting of a wick embedded in a solid, flammable substance such as wax, tallow, or paraffin)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *nūr-.
From Proto-Semitic *naśaʔ- (“lift, raise”). Compare Akkadian 𒈾𒋗𒌑𒌝 (našûm) and Arabic نَشَأَ (našaʔa).

From Proto-Semitic *našaḳ-. The root is inherited from Proto-Semitic *nšḳ. Cognate with Akkadian našāqu (“to kiss”), Ugaritic 𐎐𐎌𐎖 (nšq, “to kiss”) and Classical Syriac ܢܫܩ (nəšaq, “to kiss”). Compare Arabic نَسَقَ (nasaqa, “to arrange, coordinate”).

parole.significato: Forming words pertaining to movement, crossing, passage.
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ʕ-b-r /*ʕbr. Compare Arabic ع ب ر (ʕ b r).
See Proto-Semitic *ʕaly- and *ʕalay-. Compare Arabic ع ل ي (ʕ l y).

Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ʕmd. Compare emēdu (“to lean against; stand by; place”), 𐎓𐎎𐎄 (ʿmd, “support or foot of a wall”), and Arabic ع م د (ʕ m d), with عَمَدَ (ʕamada, “to support; stay”) and عَمُود (ʕamūd, “tent pole; column; pillar”).
Proto-Semitic *ʕaṯ̣m-, compare with Arabic ع ص م (ʕ ṣ m) and ع ظ م (ʕ ẓ m) plus Assyrian Neo-Aramaic ܥܛܡܐ (ˁṭmā).
From Proto-Semitic *ʕabar- (“to cross”). Cognate with Arabic عَبَرَ (ʕabara) and Akkadian ebēru.
From Proto-Semitic *ḡurayb- (“raven, crow”). Compare Aramaic עורבא (ʿurbaʾ), Arabic غُرَاب (ḡurāb).
From Proto-Semitic *ʕVnz- (“goat”). Cognate with Arabic عَنْز (ʕanz).
From Proto-Semitic *ʕazab-. Cognate with Arabic عَزَبَ (ʕazaba, “to be remote or absent”) and Akkadian 𒋺 (ezēbum, “to leave”).
From Proto-Semitic *ʕayn-.

parole.significato: mouse (such a rodent that is of the genus Mus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ʿakbar- (“mouse”), cognate with Arabic عَكْبَر (ʕakbar). The computing term is a semantic loan from English mouse.
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ʕalay-.

parole.significato: To ascend, rise, go up; to move from a point to a higher point.
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ʕall-, *ʕaly- (“high; height, elevation”), from Proto-Afroasiatic *ʕal-, *ʕVl(ay)- (“to be high, tall; to rise; mountain”). Related to Arabic عَلِيَ (ʕaliya, “to be high, exalted”) and عَلَى (ʕalā, “to climb”).
From Proto-Semitic *ʕiṣ́-. Related to עֵצָה ('etsá).
From Proto-Semitic *ʕaṯ̣m-. Cognate with Arabic عَظْم (ʕaẓm) and Aramaic עַטְמָא.
From Proto-Semitic *ʕaḳrab-. Compare Arabic عَقْرَب (ʕaqrab) and Classical Syriac ܥܩܪܒܐ (ʿeqarbā).

parole.significato: smoke (the visible vapor/vapour, gases, and fine particles given off by burning or smoldering material)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ʿṯn (“smoke”).
From Proto-Semitic *ʿaśr-.
From Proto-Semitic *ʿiśrū-.

parole.significato: only used in עַשְׁתֵּי עָשָׂר (ashté asár, ʿashtē ʿasár, “eleven”)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ʕaštay-. Supplanted in West Semitic by *ʔaḥad- (“lone”), whence אֶחָד (ekhád, “one”).
From Proto-Semitic *piʔat-.
From Proto-Semitic *pagr- (“body, trunk”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒇿 (pagrum) and Arabic فَجْر (fajr, “sinning, committing adultery”).
From Proto-Semitic *pay-, cognate with Aramaic פּוּמָא (pūmā), Arabic فَم (fam) / فُو (fū), Ge'ez አፍ (ʾäf), Ugaritic 𐎔 (p /⁠pû⁠/), Akkadian 𒅗 (pûm).

parole.significato: broad bean, fava bean, fava (Vicia faba)
parole.testo: Cognate with Aramaic פֹּולא (pōlā, “bean”) and Arabic فُول (fūl, “fava beans”). Ultimately perchance from Proto-Semitic *pūl- (“bean, corn, seed, grains, little pieces”); possibly distantly related to Egyptian prj (“to emerge”) and prt (“growing season”).
From Proto-Semitic *pan-. Related to the verb פָּנָה (paná, “to face”).
Cognate with Arabic فعل (faʕala, “to do”). From Proto-Semitic *paʕala.

parole.significato: fruit (a product of fertilization in a plant, specifically:)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *piry-. Cognate with Ge'ez ፍሬ (fəre) and Ugaritic 𐎔𐎗 (pr /⁠pirû⁠/).
The root is inherited from Proto-Semitic *prm. Compare Aramaic פְּרַם (“to cut apart, split”) and Arabic فَرَمَ (farama, “to chop, mince, shred”).
From Proto-Semitic *purḡūṯ- (“flea”).
From Proto-Semitic *pataḥ- (“to open”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒉿𒌅𒌑𒌝 (petûm) and Arabic فَتَحَ (fataḥa).

From Proto-Semitic *ṣ́aʔn-. Cognate with Akkadian 𒇇𒇻𒄭𒀀 (ṣēnum) and Arabic ضَأْن (ḍaʔn). After the loss of the glottal stop [ʔ] the preceding vowel was compensatorily lenghtened and became [oː] as a result of the Canaanite shift.

From Proto-Semitic *ṣ́abb-. It is likely the word originally referred to some kind of lizard (compare Classical Syriac ܥܒܐ (ʿabbā) and Arabic ضَبّ (ḍabb), both meaning “mastigure”), but its usage in reference to some type of carriage in the Bible led European Jews (who were unfamiliar with the masti
From Proto-Semitic *ṣ́abuʕ- (“hyena”). Cognate with Arabic ضَبُع (ḍabuʕ).
From Proto-Semitic *ṯ̣aby(at-). Compare Arabic ظَبْي (ẓaby) and Aramaic טַבְיָא (ṭaḇyā).
From Proto-Semitic *ṣdġ. Compare Aramaic צִדְעָא (ṣiḏʿā), Classical Syriac ܨܕܥܐ (ṣeḏʿā), from Arabic صَدْغ (ṣadḡ).
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *θ̣upr-, *θ̣ipr- (“nail, claw”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒌢 (ṣuprum) and Arabic ظُفْر (ẓufr).
From Proto-Semitic *ṯ̣ill- (“shadow”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒄑𒈪 (ṣillum, “shadow”) and Arabic ظِلّ (ẓill).

parole.significato: plate (a slightly curved but almost flat dish from which food is served or eaten)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic, akin to Arabic صَحْن (ṣaḥn, “bowl, plate”) and Ge'ez ጻሕል (ṣaḥl, “bowl, jar, pan”).
From Proto-Semitic *ṯ̣amiʔ- (“to thirst”). Compare Arabic ظَمِئَ (ẓamiʔa, “to thirst; to long”).
From Proto-Semitic [Term?]. Compare Aramaic עמר (ʿamar) and Tigrinya ጸምሪ (ṣämri).

parole.significato: Young (in the early part of life or growth).
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ṣaɣir- (“to be small, young”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒌉 (ṣeḫrum, “small, young”) and Arabic صَغِير (ṣaḡīr).
From Proto-Semitic *ṣ́arrat- (“co-wife”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒁮𒋰𒁀 (ṣerretum) and Arabic ضَرَّة (ḍarra).

parole.significato: Forming words relating to oldness, antiquity; coming before or precedence.
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Semitic *q-d-m /*qdm (“to precede, come before”). Compare with Arabic ق د م (q d m).

parole.significato: Forming words pertaining to killing and slaying
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ḳtl- (“to kill, to slay”). The Hebrew reflex of /t/ being /tˤ/ is likely due to the influence of the preceding emphatic consonant. Compare Old Aramaic ק־ת־ל, Aramaic ק־ט־ל (qṭl), Arabic ق ت ل (q t l), and Ge'ez ቀተለ (ḳätälä).

parole.significato: Forming words relating to calling or reading.
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ḳ-r-ʔ, possibly from Proto-Afroasiatic. Cognate to Arabic ق ر ء (q-r-ʔ), Classical Syriac ܩ-ܪ-ܐ (q-r-ʾ). Compare Tamahaq ăɣăr (“read, call”) and Hausa kira (“call, invite”).
From Proto-Semitic *ḳudš- (“holy”). Cognate with Arabic قُدْس (quds) and Amharic ቅዱስ (ḳədus).
From the root Proto-Semitic *q-d-m (“to precede, come before”). Compare Arabic قَدَمَ (qadama) and Classical Syriac ܩܕܡ.
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ḳadišat. By surface analysis, קָדֵשׁ (kadésh, qāḏēš, “(male) temple prostitute”) + ־ָה (-á, -ā́, “feminine suffix”).
Ultimately from Proto-Semitic *q-d-m (“to precede, come before”). Compare Aramaic קֳדָם (qŏḏām), Ge'ez ቅድመ (ḳədmä).
From Proto-Semitic *q-d-š (“holy, sacred”), see also Arabic ق د س (q d s, “untouched, free, holy”). More at Q-D-Š.
From Proto-Semitic *qayθ̣- (“summer”) Compare Aramaic קֵיטָא (qēṭā), Arabic قَيْظ (qayẓ, “oppressive heat, midsummer”), قَاظَ (qāẓa, “to be hot”).
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ḳaraʔ-.

parole.significato: horn (a hard growth of keratin that protrudes from the top of the head of certain animals, usually paired)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ḳarn- (“horn”). Cognate with Arabic قَرْن (qarn).
From Proto-Semitic *ḳarḳar-. Compare Akkadian 𒆠 (qaqqarum).
From Proto-Semitic *rayam-.

parole.significato: Root relating to herding or grazing.
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Semitic *raʕay-.
From Proto-Semitic *raʔš-. Cognate with Akkadian 𒊕 (rēšum) and Arabic رَأْس (raʔs).
From Proto-Semitic *rabb-.
From Proto-Semitic *rigl-.
From Proto-Semitic *raḫil- (“ewe”). Cognate with Aramaic רַחְלָא (raḥlā) (absolutive: רְחֵל (rəḥēl)), Arabic رَخِل (raḵil) (also رِخْل (riḵl)).
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *raḥim- (“womb”). Compare Arabic رَحِم (raḥim, “womb”), Akkadian rēmum (“womb; mercy”).
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *rayam-.

From Proto-Semitic *ramaz- (“to wink, sign, signal”). Compare Aramaic רְמַז (“to indicate, make signs, beckon, wink”), Classical Syriac ܪܡܙܐ (remzā, “sign, hint, gesture”), Arabic رَمْز (ramz, “symbol, emblem, cypher, code”), Ge'ez (through metathesis) ረዘመ (razama, “to wink”).

parole.significato: Shin or sin: the twenty-first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, after ר and before ת.
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *šinn- (“tooth”), the source of שן. The association of "tooth" with this letter was the result of folk etymology and based on the corresponding Phoenician letter, 𐤔 (š), having a shape resembling a tooth. The letter originally depicted a composite bow, which usually has the tips c
From Proto-Semitic *šaḥ(a)r- (“dawn, morning”). Cognate with Arabic root س ح ر (s ḥ r).

parole.significato: Forming words pertaining to completion, wholeness, peace.
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *š-l-m. Cognate with Arabic root س ل م (s l m).
From Proto-Semitic *šamaʕ-.

parole.significato: Forms words meaning to judge, or to create order, as in to arrange.
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ṯapāṭ- (“to pass judgment”). Compare with Ugaritic 𐎘𐎔𐎉 (ṯpṭ)
From Proto-Semitic *šabṭ-.
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *šabʕatum.
From Proto-Semitic *šabʿū-.

parole.significato: break (a location where something has been broken)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ṯabar- (“to break”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒊺𒁉𒀸 (šebērum) and Arabic ثَبَرَ (ṯabara, “to destroy”).
From Proto-Semitic *ṯdʾ (“breast, pap, teat”). Cognate with Arabic ثَدْي (ṯady, “breast”) and Aramaic תַּדָּא (“breast”).

parole.significato: garlic (a plant, Allium sativum, related to the onion, having a pungent bulb much used in cooking)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ṯūm-; cognate with Akkadian 𒋧 (šūmū), Aramaic תּוּמָא (tūmā), Arabic ثُوم (ṯūm).

parole.significato: fox (the red fox, a small carnivore (Vulpes vulpes) with red or silver fur)
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *ṯaʕlab- (“fox”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒈜𒀀 (šēlebum) and Arabic ثَعْلَب (ṯaʕlab). Compare also Yemeni Arabic ثَعَلْ.
From Proto-Semitic *ṯawr- (“bull, ox”). Cognate with Arabic ثَوْر (ṯawr).

parole.significato: root (the part of a plant, generally underground, that anchors and supports the plant body, absorbs and stores water an…
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *šurš-.
From Proto-Semitic *šaḥ(a)r- (“dawn, morning”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒀉𒄘𒍣𒂵 (šērum) and Arabic سَحَر (saḥar).

From Proto-Semitic *šu(n)bulat- (“spike”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒋗𒁍𒌌𒌈 (šubultum, “ear of wheat”), Ugaritic 𐎌𐎁𐎍𐎚 (šblt, “ear of grain”), Aramaic שׁוּבַּלְתָּא/שִׁבַּלְתָּא (šubbaltā/šibbaltā), Classical Syriac ܫܒܠܬܐ (šeb(b)eltāʼ, “ear of grain; flow of a river”), Old South Arabian 𐩪𐩨𐩡𐩩 (s¹blt, “ear o
From Proto-Semitic *śaʕr- (“hair”). Cognate with Arabic شعر.
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *šidṯatum.
From Proto-Semitic *šidθū-.
From Proto-Semitic *šikar- (“alcoholic drink”). Compare Arabic سَكِرَ (sakira, “to get drunk, to become intoxicated”) and سَكَر (sakar, “intoxicant, wine”).
From Proto-Semitic *ṯalg- (“snow”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒊭𒀠𒄖𒌝 (šalgum) and Arabic ثَلْج (ṯalj).
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ṯalāṯatum.
From Proto-Semitic *śalāθū-.
From Proto-Semitic *šim-, from Proto-Afroasiatic *sim- (“name”). Cognate with Arabic اسم (ism, “name”) and Aramaic שְׁמָא (šəmā).

From Proto-Semitic *śimaʔl-. Cognate with Arabic شِمَال (šimāl), Akkadian 𒆏 (šumēlum), Aramaic סְמָלָא (səmālā), שְׂמָאלָא (śəmālā), ܣܸܡܵܠܵܐ (semmālā), Ugaritic 𐎌𐎎𐎀𐎍 (šmảl). The north sense derives from the direction being on the left side facing the sunrise, this sense also exists in Arabic.
From Proto-Semitic *ṯamāniy-.
From Proto-Semitic *θamāniyū-.
From Proto-Semitic [Term?]. Cognate with Ugaritic 𐎌𐎎𐎃 (šmḫ, “to be glad, rejoice”).
From Proto-Semitic *šamāy-.
From Proto-Semitic *šamn-.

parole.significato: to hear, to be able to hear
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *šamiʕ-. Cognate with Arabic سَمِعَ (samiʕa, “to hear”).
From Proto-Semitic *śamš-.

From Proto-Semitic *šinn-. By surface analysis either derived from שָׁנַן (shanán, “to be sharp, to sharpen”) or a primitive word with no verbal root as its origin. Cognates include Arabic سِنّ (sinn), Akkadian 𒅗 (šinnum), Aramaic שִׁנָּא (šinā’), and Ge'ez ስን (sən).

parole.significato: year (the time it takes for the Earth to complete one revolution around the Sun)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Semitic *šanat-. Cognate to Arabic سَنَة (sana), Ugaritic 𐎌𐎐𐎚 (šnt /⁠šanatu⁠/).
From Proto-Semitic *ṯin-.
Derived from Proto-Semitic *śaʕr-. Cognate with Arabic شَعْر / شَعَر (šaʕr / šaʕar, “hair”), Ge'ez ጸጕር (ṣägʷr).
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *śapat- (“lip”).
From the root שׁ־ק־ל (sh-q-l), in the pa`ál conjugation. From Proto-Semitic *ṯql (“to weigh; burden, weight”); cognate with Arabic ثقل and Aramaic תקל.
From Proto-Semitic *śarār (“to rule”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒊩𒈗 (šarratum, “queen”) and Arabic سرر (“to bring joy and delight”).
From Proto-Semitic *tiʔin-. Cognate to Arabic تين (tīn).
From Proto-Semitic *tihām-. Cognate with Akkadian 𒀀𒀊𒁀 (tiāmtum, “sea; Tiamat”).

parole.significato: tell (a hill or mound, originally and especially in the Middle East, over or consisting of the ruins of ancient settlem…
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *tall- (“hill”).
From Proto-Semitic *tišʿ-.
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *tišʿū-. Cognate with Arabic تِسْعُونَ (tisʕūna).
